- `apps/web/src/index.css:441`: The global hit-area rule gives no extra width to a control that is 44 px tall or more but narrower than 44 px, and spec 47 would report that control as passing, so the spec cannot fail a control that is too narrow, which the issue requires. (For a box with height h >= 44, `top`/`bottom: clamp((h-44)/2, (h-44)*1000, 50%)` resolves to 50%, so the `::before` is 0 px tall. `left`/`right: min(0px, (w-44)/2)` widen it to 44 px, but a 0-px-tall box catches no tap. In 47-tap-areas.cy.ts `hitBox` merges the pseudo's left and right edges whatever its height (`hit.left = min(hit.left, origin.x + x)`, with `h = 0` changing only the vertical side). A 30x50 button would therefore measure 44 px across while it still takes taps over only 30 px. The issue's spec bullet asks for a failure 'below the minimum in either dimension'. The CSS comment ('left and right reach out only by what the width falls short') is wrong whenever the box is tall. The ruling's first paragraph ('every interactive element smaller than 44x44 ... gets a hit area of at least that size') also disagrees with its own 'a control shorter than the minimum' paragraph and the README's 'shorter than that'. At minimum, `hitBox` should skip a pseudo with zero width or height; then the CSS should cover tall, narrow controls, or the ruling should say plainly that it does not.)

# #2122: Patch: 44x44 tap areas for small controls on phones
Opened by @squishy-squooby.

Part of #2036. This is a patch of its own: it goes live when it merges and builds on `main` beside the tracker's other parts.

## What

This is the "hit slop" tip. `index.css` has a single 44 px minimum. On the phone layout (390×844), many controls are smaller: activate badges, close buttons, pile counts, the gear, the emote and log toggles, chips in pickers.

- **The minimum.** Every interactive element (`button`, `a[href]`, `[role=button]`, `input`, `select`, `[tabindex="0"]`) whose box is smaller than 44×44 CSS px gets a hit area of at least that size. Keep the minimum as one custom property in `index.css` and one TS constant for the spec.
- **How.** Use an absolutely positioned `::before` with a negative inset, centred on the control, so nothing in the layout moves.
- **Neighbours.** Where two neighbours' hit areas would overlap, they split the gap, so no hit area ever covers another control.
- **Exempt:**
  - inline links inside a paragraph;
  - cards, whose boxes are already larger;
  - controls under an open modal's scrim.
- **The spec.** A new e2e spec next to `46` visits the board (a practice game) and every menu `46` visits, at 390×844. It measures each interactive element's hit box (its own box together with its `::before`) and fails below the minimum in either dimension, naming the element's testid. Spec `46` itself is unchanged.

## Done when

- The new e2e spec and `46` are green.
- Gates: `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`, `pnpm --dir apps/web test`, `pnpm exec eslint apps/web e2e`.

## Ground rules (from #2036)

- Read `apps/web/README.md` and `e2e/README.md` first. CLAUDE.md rule 7: nothing here predicts, enforces or reveals game state.
- Every number is a named constant (rule 9).
- If SPEC §10 doesn't already decide a behaviour, add a ruling note numbered from this issue's own block (`docs/issues-and-patches.md`, Ruling numbers), with its proving test named after it.
- The PR closes this issue, says `Part of #2036`, and carries one `## Player note` line.

type Box = { left: number; top: number; right: number; bottom: number };
type Control = { el: Element; name: string; own: Box; shown: Box; hit: Box; exempt: boolean };

const boxOf = (el: Element): Box => {
  const { left, top, right, bottom } = el.getBoundingClientRect();
  return { left, top, right, bottom };

const union = (a: Box, b: Box): Box => ({ left: Math.min(a.left, b.left), top: Math.min(a.top, b.top), right: Math.max(a.right, b.right), bottom: Math.max(a.bottom, b.bottom) });
/** How far two boxes overlap across and down (negative: the gap between them). */
const overlap = (a: Box, b: Box) => ({ x: Math.min(a.right, b.right) - Math.max(a.left, b.left), y: Math.min(a.bottom, b.bottom) - Math.max(a.top, b.top) });

/** A checkbox's or a radio's labels, which toggle it: part of its box and of its hit area. The tag, not `instanceof`: the page is another window. */
function labelsOf(el: Element): Element[] {
  const input = el as HTMLInputElement;
  return el.tagName === "INPUT" && (input.type === "checkbox" || input.type === "radio") && input.labels !== null ? Array.from(input.labels) : [];

/** `el`'s own box with each absolutely placed ::before and ::after that takes taps, in each dimension its overflow leaves open, and its labels'. */
function hitBox(win: Window, el: Element): Box {
  const style = win.getComputedStyle(el);
  let hit = boxOf(el);
  const origin = { x: hit.left + parseFloat(style.borderLeftWidth), y: hit.top + parseFloat(style.borderTopWidth) };
  for (const which of ["::before", "::after"]) {
    const p = win.getComputedStyle(el, which);
    if (p.content === "none" || p.content === "normal" || p.position !== "absolute" || style.position === "static" || p.pointerEvents === "none") continue;
    // A centring translate (inspectable.css's pile band) shifts the box; the rest of a transform is ignored.
    const shift = new DOMMatrixReadOnly(p.transform === "none" ? undefined : p.transform);
    const [x, y, w, h] = [parseFloat(p.left) + shift.e, parseFloat(p.top) + shift.f, parseFloat(p.width), parseFloat(p.height)];

    if (style.overflowX === "visible") hit = { ...hit, left: Math.min(hit.left, origin.x + x), right: Math.max(hit.right, origin.x + x + w) };
    if (style.overflowY === "visible") hit = { ...hit, top: Math.min(hit.top, origin.y + y), bottom: Math.max(hit.bottom, origin.y + y + h) };
  }
  return labelsOf(el).reduce((sum, label) => union(sum, hitBox(win, label)), hit);

/** The part of `el` the window and its clipping ancestors show; null when none is (scrolled out of its region). */
function shownBox(win: Window, el: Element): Box | null {
  let shown = { ...boxOf(el) };
  shown = { left: Math.max(shown.left, 0), top: Math.max(shown.top, 0), right: Math.min(shown.right, win.innerWidth), bottom: Math.min(shown.bottom, win.innerHeight) };

    const style = win.getComputedStyle(up);
    const clip = boxOf(up);
    if (style.overflowX !== "visible") shown = { ...shown, left: Math.max(shown.left, clip.left), right: Math.min(shown.right, clip.right) };
    if (style.overflowY !== "visible") shown = { ...shown, top: Math.max(shown.top, clip.top), bottom: Math.min(shown.bottom, clip.bottom) };

/** Its testid, or what it is and the nearest testid round it. */
function nameOf(el: Element): string {

/** The controls a tap reaches now: shown, taking pointer events, and inside the topmost open modal if there is one. */
function controlsOf(win: Window): Control[] {

    controls.push({ el, name: nameOf(el), own, shown, hit: hitBox(win, el), exempt: el.matches(EXEMPT) });

 * centre on each side, or halfway to a neighbour nearer than that (the split); and it covers no
 * neighbour's shown box. A neighbour is another control, neither holding the other, whose box does

    const others = controls.filter((n) => {
      const o = overlap(c.own, n.own);
      return n !== c && !n.el.contains(c.el) && !c.el.contains(n.el) && (o.x <= SLACK_PX || o.y <= SLACK_PX);

    const [cx, cy] = [(c.own.left + c.own.right) / 2, (c.own.top + c.own.bottom) / 2];
    const reach = { left: cx - half, top: cy - half, right: cx + half, bottom: cy + half };
